items.title: Rag, Lich, Aya or Tarim?
items.text:
Rag, Lich, Aya or Tarim?
Hi, have been playing in wild for 4 months now. I now own Genn and Baku, Tharussian, Patches, Loatheb, Mecha'thun, Leeroy , Thekal, Soularium, Reno, Brann and SIr Finley as my 'playable' legendaries. As a F2P player, I hope to expand my options and hope to craft one of the four listed in the title above. I think rag is solid but a bit inconsistant, Lich is ok but is slightly weaker, aya only sees play in 2 decks and tarim is a class card and only helps in aggro. I'm torn between these four, what do you guys suggest?
I have even shaman, odd rogue, odd paladin, pirate warrior, inner fire priest, raza priest, evenlock, midrange hunter, aggro druid, zoolock. I hope to have a flexible legendary to fit in those decks.
I already have kazakus. Thanks for your suggestions.
I'm leaning rag and lich, and who do you think is better?
Likkim is still run in aggro variants.
Wouldn't it fail as when the Mecha'thun dies it does not trigger as dorian is not yet dead?
Sorry my bad. I remeber now that you can trigger mechathun by poison seeds.

I believe that you can get by without lich king in evenlock. Just sub in a flexible card like dark peddler, anklebiter, wrathguard, shadow flame or spell breaker and it works just as fine. most games are decided in turns 4-7, so lich is not that important. if you want a big finisher rag would be better.
when the the end sign shows up and all rebels die is it really the end?
I would like to have a discrete ending like universal paperclips, which would feel more satisfying. But that's just me.
Why holy nova? Its seems weak. And why no fungalmancer for an aggro deck?
I still don't see the value behind it. after all, consecration costs 1 less, still isn't used in aggro pally.

Some cards like swordsmith and priestess seem super weak man, without enchanter its trash, and even with it it won't be super good. I highly recommend shadowbomber and less situational 2 drops such as radiant elemental. Perhaps also velen's chosen and spawn of shadows?
Played since gvg: that explains a lot.
I'm playing purify priest in rank 3, having a blast. Yes, we are playing the same game.
Dr. Boom's scheme -- the desperation is real.

Competitive spirit is ok considering you have never surrender, increasing your survivability of your dudes, but 4 one drops is a recipe for disaster. I would recommend cutting 1 fungal and both spirits for at least 3 drops. The two mainstream options are double argent squire + firefly or double deckhand + patches. Personally, I prefer pirates as it is slightly more powerful and patches reduces chances of dead draws, but double argent squire has fewer low-rolls and divine shield synergy, so if you don't have patches the alternative is completely fine. For the second option, also cut one maul for rallying blade since divine shields are much more abundant.

Silence priest seems fun. I also want to see the mulligan guide!

The even shaman decks seem too heavy to my liking, why are all these players go so top-heavy in most decks in this report?
Please no, people will stop playing wild. I don't want to wait for 5 minutes just for a game. the player base is already small.

>So I think it's better to criticize the phrase as a phrase and not the person who said that.

Well said indeed! It is refreshing that someone does not devolve into identity politics nowadays. Just like Nazis knew the importance of leisure and made some medical discoveries like the carcinogenic properties of tobacco; what they said was true. It does not lessen the severity of the atrocities they have done though.
He thought that fungalmancer was an aura effect...
I disagree. Zombie chow is a premium 1 drop. I would certainly pick it over both of them.

I also pushed to rank 1 with it. I'd say it is very well rounded, and with even shaman less popular, it is very well suited for the meta. odd paladins are a 45-55 matchup personally, just play around blessing of might and you'll be fine.
Craft patches. it is also used in odd rogue, odd paladin and aggro druids. definitely a future proof craft.

I was initially very hesitant, and procrastinated crafting it. I would be thinking, 'am I spending 1600 dust on a WISP?????' then I realised its importance on board control and my winrate against aggro skyrocketed from 'akin to facing even shaman' to 50/50.
Priests now a midrange. one drops are still good. heck, it trades better than most 2 drops!

I agree. Start with the 'fantastic four' of Baku, patches, leeroy and loatheb to play every aggro deck. then move to genn as midrange, then the control package of brann, Zola, kazakus, reno and dirty rat. these neutral cards give you the greatest value as you can play multiple decks with them.
That was very cool of you!

Fellow pirate warrior. What do you think about replacing one upgrade with loatheb? I've been trying it, and is working ok. The main reason is to prevent dead draws and improve against control. My win rate against aggro doesn't seem to have diminished. What do you think?
